title: Manatee County School Board, District 5
what_it_does: School board members set the district budget and school-tax rate, hire the superintendent (where appointed), approve school boundaries, curriculum policy and construction, and set district policies. Nonpartisan.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); both candidates are marked Qualified, which for a nonpartisan seat means the August vote did not produce a majority winner (or the seat is decided only in November). Check the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Camden "Cam" Bedinghaus
candidates.occupation: Director, Turning Point USA Manatee County; independent journalist
candidates.background: Bedinghaus, 23, is a Manatee County native and district graduate who finished an economics degree at the University of South Florida in May 2026, where he served on a campus council that allocated budgets. He directs the Turning Point USA hub in Manatee County and writes for a conservative local news outlet. He was the only District 5 candidate to qualify by petition and finished second in the Aug. 18, 2026 primary with about 34%.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

school_books.summary: At the Oct. 1 League forum Bedinghaus said sexually explicit or otherwise age-inappropriate material should be removed, noting parents can still buy such books themselves. His campaign site says parents and teachers, rather than bureaucrats or activists, should decide what happens in the classroom.
school_books.quote: then I don't see a problem with removing that.

teacher_pay.summary: Bedinghaus proposes teacher bonuses tied to student progress, to be paid by redirecting money from district programs that are not producing results and, he said at the Oct. 1 League forum, from about $2.4 million the county returned to the district.
teacher_pay.quote: I plan on introducing incentive based bonuses based on student progress.

taxes.summary: At the Oct. 1 League forum Bedinghaus said he supported the 2024 one-mill school property tax and expects some level of renewal, while first putting returned tax money toward teacher bonuses and cutting programs that are not producing results.

education_choice.summary: At the Oct. 1 League forum Bedinghaus said parents have the ultimate right to choose where their children go to school and called Florida's school choice a gift, while saying the district must make its public schools the best choice so families come back.
education_choice.quote: they have the ultimate right of where their children go to school. And that's an amazing thing, amazing gift we have here in Florida

candidates.name: Jonathan Mullis
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Physical therapist; owner and CEO, Physical Therapy Doctors of Florida
candidates.background: Mullis holds a doctorate in physical therapy from Simmons University and ran a practice in Massachusetts before moving to Manatee County in 2017, where he founded Physical Therapy Doctors of Florida. The son of two teachers, he has two daughters in Manatee schools, is president of the Bradenton Kiwanis Club and sits on the Manatee Tiger Bay Club board. He led the Aug. 18, 2026 District 5 primary with about 35%.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

education_choice.summary: Mixed. Mullis calls himself a strong supporter of school choice and lists it on his campaign site, but at the Oct. 1 League forum he said he does not agree with the Legislature's removal of the scholarship income limits, which sends checks to families already paying for private or home school, and wants the program modified.
education_choice.quote: I'd like to see the legislature make some modifications to it.

school_safety.summary: His site says he supports strong safety measures including school resource officers and clear discipline policies to maintain order and respect; it does not mention counselors or mental-health staffing.
school_safety.quote: Supporting strong safety measures, including resource officers

sources.title: Vote Mullis - Manatee County School Board District 5

school_books.summary: At the Oct. 1 League forum Mullis said he is not in favor of removing books entirely but wants library books to be age-appropriate, possibly restricting some to older grades, and that the district should follow its review policy promptly. He has also said the district should follow its existing policies.
school_books.quote: I'm not a fan of taking the books out completely, but I definitely think we need to have books age appropriate.

taxes.quote: I will most likely support something.
